comparisons.error_analysis: The review detector checks only 'systematic review', 'scoping review', 'meta-analysis', or 'review article' in the title. It misses the abstract's explicit 'This review'. The word 'patient' then triggers the clinical label. High conjunction density also overstates extraction complexity for a broad narrative review.
The core type and route are correct. RESULTS and CONCLUSION labels are missed because the converted abstract stores section labels inline rather than after a newline.
The operational route is correct. The same inline structured-heading parsing bug causes the only profile mismatch.
Exact match on the four evaluated fields, although the single-label profile does not preserve the accompanying in-vitro hepatocyte modality.

The precedence rule assigns 'computational' as soon as machine learning/diagnostic model language appears. It therefore masks scRNA-seq plus Western blot/qPCR validation in human fibrotic liver tissue. The incorrect primary label downgrades a genuinely multimodal article from DEEP to STANDARD.

interpretation: This five-document audit is diagnostic, not a statistically stable estimate. It demonstrates concrete label-precedence, mixed-design representation, and structured-heading parsing failures that can change downstream evidence policy and tool routing.
